What the marks mean

The mark in the corner says what you see.

ARCHIVEthe archive and year

Real film or photograph from the archive, unaltered beyond trims, crops and slow moves.

RECONSTRUCTEDarchive 1947 upscaled

Archive film or photographs changed in a way that matters: colourised, re-timed, stabilised, or enlarged by a computer model. The mark names the change.

AI-GENERATEDcontext

Made by a computer model: places, weather, objects. Never people, never a recorded event.

DRAWNfrom a census table

A map or diagram drawn by us from named data.

VOID DOCUMENT

Text on black: titles, chapter cards, and where the record is silent.

The Partition of India

1946 to today, told with the public record

Two nations were born in the same week of August 1947. On the night of 14 August, in Delhi, Nehru told the Constituent Assembly that not far from Delhi, big cities were ablaze. A narrator tells it as one story, with readings from the record: the clock, the line, the two midnights, the roads beside the canals, Delhi itself, and those who stayed.

Every reading is word for word from its source, sometimes in part (marked ...). This film shows no bodies or killing.
